title: Multimodal Models: Images, Audio and Text
summary: Multimodal models turn pictures and sound into sequences of vectors the same transformer can read. This lesson counts the tokens an image, a minute of audio or a video produces, derives the CLIP contrastive loss, shows how a vision encoder is wired into a language model, and budgets what all of this costs in context and compute.
objectives: Compute how many patch tokens an image produces and the size of the patch-embedding layer
Write the CLIP symmetric contrastive loss and evaluate it on a small similarity matrix
Describe how a vision encoder, a projector and an LLM are combined and trained in stages
Estimate audio tokens per second for spectrogram encoders and neural codecs
Budget the context and compute of images, audio and video in a request
prerequisites: You should know how a transformer treats a sequence of vectors ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)), what embeddings are ([Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings)), and how context length drives cost ([Context Windows, Prefill and the KV Cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache)). Softmax and cross-entropy are used as in earlier lessons.
